Description: Selects the AzerothCore source tree and compatible module track. Playerbots presets keep the required core fork and module branch paired. Run Update after changing this setting.
For a custom distribution, sets the HTTPS Git repository containing the AzerothCore-compatible core. Empty uses the official repository for the selected family.
For a custom distribution, sets a branch, tag, or commit SHA. Empty uses master for standard AzerothCore or Playerbot for the Playerbots fork.
For Playerbots custom, sets the HTTPS Git repository for the Playerbots module. Empty uses mod-playerbots/mod-playerbots.
For Playerbots custom, sets the module branch, tag, or commit SHA. Keep it compatible with the selected core ref.

Optional comma-separated GitHub repositories compiled as modules. Format: owner/repository or owner/repository@branch-or-tag. Example: azerothcore/mod-autobalance@master,azerothcore/mod-individual-progression. Changes trigger a clean rebuild.
Sets the CMake build type. RelWithDebInfo is recommended because it keeps useful symbols while using optimized code.
Maximum parallel compiler jobs. 0 automatically uses up to four jobs. Lower this if the AMP container runs out of memory while compiling.
Deletes the CMake build cache before every update. Distribution, module, build-type, and CMake-option changes already trigger a clean build automatically.
Optional whitespace-separated CMake -D options. Values containing spaces are not supported. Options are passed without shell evaluation.
Downloads compatible enUS AzerothCore client data (dbc, maps, vmaps, mmaps, and Cameras). Disable only when supplying extracted data manually in dist/bin.
GitHub release tag from wowgaming/client-data. v20.0 is the current default. Use another published tag only when a deliberately pinned historical core requires it.
Name shown in the Wrath of the Lich King realm list. AzerothCore limits this field to 32 characters.
Selects the address advertised to remote clients. Automatic uses AMP's detected external IP. Manual accepts an IP address or DNS hostname.
Public IP address or DNS hostname advertised when Manual is selected. For LAN-only play, use the AMP host LAN address.
Address advertised to clients detected on the local subnet. Set this to the AMP host's LAN IP for split local/public access.
Subnet mask used by AzerothCore to decide whether a client receives the local or public realm address.
Maximum number of real player sessions accepted by worldserver. Playerbots are managed separately by the module.

When enabled, AzerothCore public, party, raid, guild, channel, and whisper chat log lines are exposed to AMP so its activity feed can display chat. Disabled by default for privacy and because Playerbots can generate substantial chat traffic. Addon-channel traffic remains suppressed.

Polling interval for the Playerbots-only Bots Online AMP metric. This setting shares the main Playerbots page. Standard AzerothCore distributions do not publish a custom metric; AMP native Active Users remains available for real players.
Message displayed after a player logs in.
DefaultValue: Welcome to an AzerothCore server powered by AMP!

Description: Sets AzerothCore GameType. Free-for-all PvP is a custom mode displayed as PvP in the realm list.
Starting level for newly created non-heroic characters.
Multiplier for experience gained from kills.
Multiplier for experience gained from quests.
Multiplier for experience gained from exploration.
Multiplier for money dropped by creatures.
Global multiplier for item drops. Individual quality and source rates can still be changed in worldserver.conf.
Multiplier for reputation gained from kills and quests.
Gold given to newly created characters. The launcher converts this to AzerothCore copper units (1 gold = 10,000 copper).
Controls which characters skip their race intro cinematic. 0 uses the normal client behavior, 1 skips after another character of that race has seen it, and 2 always skips.

EnumValues.1: Skip after first character of the race

Description: Optional message shown to a character when entering the world. Empty uses no custom start message.
Shows AzerothCore server information to players when they log in.
Multiplier for honor gains.
Multiplier for arena-point gains.
Multiplier for normal quest money rewards.
Multiplier for bonus money awarded when a maximum-level character completes a quest that would otherwise grant experience.
Scales health for normal, elite, rare-elite, rare, and world-boss creatures together. Use advanced worldserver.conf editing when different creature ranks need different values.
Scales melee damage for normal, elite, rare-elite, rare, and world-boss creatures together.
Scales spell damage for normal, elite, rare-elite, rare, and world-boss creatures together.
When enabled, resetting talents does not charge the normal escalating gold cost.
Allows players to enter instances without meeting their normal level requirement.
Allows entry to raid instances without being in a raid group. Useful for small private realms.
Local server hour used for daily instance-reset scheduling. Valid values are 0 through 23.

DisplayName: Allow Both Factions On One Account
Description: Allows Horde and Alliance characters to coexist on the same account on PvP realms.
Enables cross-faction chat, channels, groups, guilds, arenas, and the shared auction house as one convenient private-realm switch.
Interval between automatic character saves. Lower values reduce possible progress loss but increase database writes.
Optional extra save triggers using AzerothCore’s bitmask: 1 on logout, 2 on group changes, and 4 on bind-to-instance. Values can be combined; 7 enables all three.
Enables AzerothCore’s Warden client-integrity checks.
Rejects modified clients whose version information does not match the expected Wrath 3.3.5a client.
Number of failed login attempts before a temporary ban. 0 disables automatic wrong-password bans.
Duration of a wrong-password ban. AzerothCore treats 0 as permanent when the attempt threshold is enabled.
Selects whether automatic wrong-password protection bans the source IP or the account.
Adds failed login attempts to the authentication log.

Enables Proxy Protocol v2 on both authserver and worldserver. Enable this only when a compatible proxy or load balancer is configured to send the protocol; direct clients cannot connect correctly otherwise.
Allows AzerothCore to store player IP addresses in its databases and logs. Disable where local privacy policy requires it.
Enables the built-in IP-based player-action logging script when supported by the selected core.
Seconds without world-loop progress before AzerothCore terminates a stuck worldserver. 0 disables the freeze detector.
Number of world map update threads. Leave at 1 for small servers; increase carefully on CPUs with spare cores.
Number of network worker threads used by worldserver.
Threads used for signal handling, remote access, database keep-alive, freeze checks, and world-socket networking.
zlib compression level for world traffic. Valid values are 1 through 9; higher values use more CPU.
Portable Oracle MySQL release stream. AzerothCore requires MySQL 8.0 or newer; 8.4 LTS is recommended.
Optional exact Oracle MySQL version, such as 8.4.6. Empty automatically resolves the latest patch in the selected release stream.
Memory reserved for MySQL's InnoDB buffer pool. Playerbots and larger populations benefit from a larger value, but the AMP container must have enough RAM.
Playerbots distributions only. Enables randomly generated bots that populate and play in the world.
Playerbots distributions only. Minimum target number of random bots.
Playerbots distributions only. Maximum target number of random bots. Keep this greater than or equal to Minimum Random Bots.
Playerbots distributions only. Random bots log out after all real players leave and return after a player logs in.
Playerbots distributions only. Maximum number of bots one player may control simultaneously.
Playerbots distributions only. Number of accounts reserved for bots created by the addclass command.
Playerbots distributions only. 0 lets the module calculate the required number of random-bot accounts automatically.
Playerbots distributions only. Automatically logs a player’s alternate characters in as controllable altbots when the player connects.
Allows players to invite and control altbots from their own account.
Allows players to invite and control eligible bots from their guild.
Allows linked trusted accounts to share altbot control.
When Disable Bots Without Real Players is enabled, delay after a real player logs in before random bots start logging in.
When Disable Bots Without Real Players is enabled, delay after the final real player leaves before random bots log out.
Number of random bots the manager may process for login, logout, or updates in each manager cycle. Lower this if bot population changes cause lag spikes.
Seconds between random-bot manager update cycles.
Controls who may invite bots to groups: GM only, level-based acceptance, or always accept.
Allows non-GM players to create temporary class bots through the Playerbots addclass command.
Target number of guilds generated for random bots.
Maximum membership for generated random-bot guilds. The module enforces its own minimum.

DisplayName: Allow Random Bots To Invite Players
Description: Allows random bots to invite real players to groups, raids, or guilds.
Allows random bots to talk in world and guild channels. Disable to reduce chat noise.
Allows random bots to perform social emotes.
Enables Playerbots’ generated broadcast messages.
Git ref used when AMP downloads this template's installer and launcher scripts. Keep main normally; use the same feature branch only while testing an unmerged template update.
